subject: Request: short-term hold and backup purge cadence for upcoming audit
messages:
From: Emma Blake <emma@corahealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Data retention request for upcoming SOC audit

Hannah —

Thanks for taking this. CoraHealth has an external SOC readiness audit scheduled for the week of 2026-07-26. The auditor team has asked us to place a narrow temporary hold on deletion of records and logs for three specific product streams (auth, payment, and callback logs) covering the period 2026-06-01 -> 2026-07-25 while they complete evidence collection.

We understand this is an exception to the normal purge cadence and we want to make the ask as surgical as possible:
- Temporary non-deletion window: 7/12/2026 — 7/26/2026 (retain items created between 6/1–7/25)
- Backup snapshot freeze: please avoid the scheduled backup purge that would remove snapshots containing the evidence window during the hold
- Scope: auth.*, payment.transactions.*, callbacks.* (logs + archived snapshots)

I've attached the auditor request. Can Redwood confirm whether we can implement a scoped short-term hold (no longer than 14 days) and whether there are any subprocessor or cross-border implications we need to surface? We also need a clear timeline for when normal purge resumes and how we'll confirm deletion afterward.

Attachment: CoraHealth_Audit_Request.pdf (PDF, 84 KB)

Thanks,
Emma Blake
Head of Compliance, CoraHealth
emma@corahealth.com

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Emma Blake <emma@corahealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data retention request for upcoming SOC audit

Emma —

Appreciate the clear scope. Quick read: we can usually support scoped, time-bound holds; I want to confirm the exact mechanisms and any downstream implications before we lock timeline. Internally cc'd karthik (infra) for implementation and kimberly (legal) for DPA amendment/record.

High-level plan I propose:
1) Scoped hold config: configure a retention exception that marks the three log prefixes as protected for the named window. This will prevent scheduled deletion jobs and snapshot pruning from removing related objects.
2) Backup purge pause: pause the next scheduled snapshot prune that would run during the hold window and flag affected backup sets for manual review.
3) Evidence handoff: once audit team confirms collection is complete, we run a shrink/verification job and provide a signed deletion statement.

Questions for CoraHealth: small asks to make this low-friction for us:
- Confirm whether the hold must apply to data stored in any EU regions or is US-only
- Are the auditors going to request copies (exfil) or just verify in-place evidence?

I'll defer to karthik for timing/ops details, and to kimberly for any DPA/subprocessor notice we need to send.

—Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Manager, Data Compliance — Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Emma Blake <emma@corahealth.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 13:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data retention request for upcoming SOC audit

Emma / Hannah —

Operational note from infra: we can implement the hold with our exception tagging flow. A couple of implementation details and constraints to set expectations:

- Retention tagging: we'll add a short-term "audit_hold_cora_20260712" tag to objects that match the prefixes you listed. This tag will block automated delete and snapshot prune flows.
- Backup snapshot handling: snapshots that have already been queued for prune can be pulled into a manual-keep list, but that requires a human ops window. If you need us to pause the automated prune for the whole backup set, give us the snapshot IDs or the date range and we'll schedule the pause.
- Subprocessor considerations: some of the backup lifecycle and long-term cold snapshots are stored in a partner cold-archive subprocessor (ArchVault). Pausing purge there requires an explicit change request and 24–48 hours lead time; we have to notify them and they may ask for a formal DPA amendment or written authorization from CoraHealth to retain beyond standard SLA.
- Cross-border risk: if any of the snapshots/archives are stored in EU or APAC buckets, the hold could flag a cross-border export if auditors request copies. Please confirm the region scope.

Estimated times:
- Tagging + block on deletion: 2–4 hours once lists are provided
- Snapshot prune pause request to ArchVault: 1–2 business days for acknowledgement; 48–72 hours for confirmation depending on their backlog
- Final verification & deletion statement (once audit completes): 1 business day to run verification and prepare signed statement

Operation items I need from you (Emma): list of exact prefixes, list of affected snapshot dates/IDs (if you have them), point of contact for ArchVault authorization.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
SRE Lead — Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Emma Blake <emma@corahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data retention request for upcoming SOC audit

Emma / team —

We can support the temporary hold but will need a brief DPA amendment addendum that documents: scope (prefixes), retention window, confirmation that CoraHealth authorizes Redwood to request ArchVault to hold snapshots beyond standard retention, and an agreement on deletion attestation after the hold. I've drafted a short amendment (see attached) that Redwood legal can sign once CoraHealth countersigns. We will also need a named authorization (CoraHealth legal or compliance) to make the subprocessor request on your behalf.

Next steps I propose:
- CoraHealth reviews the attached one-page addendum and returns a signed copy via DocuSign
- Once signed, karthik can file the change request with ArchVault and we will tag the objects.
- Redwood will produce a signed deletion certificate within 24h of audit confirmation and file it to the shared evidence folder.

Attachment: proposed-dpa-amendment.docx (DOCX, 16 KB)

Minor legal notes:
- This addendum is narrowly scoped and time-boxed; it explicitly says no change to ongoing retention policy beyond the specified window
- If auditors request copies that require cross-border transfers we will need an export authorization (we can attach a template to the amendment)

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Data — Redwood Inference
